display.purpose: Page h1s, two lines rising from blur; 68px desktop, 60px small, 32-41.6px phone.

headline.purpose: Section h2s via the section head; 48px desktop, 38.4/30.4px smaller. 56px for long detail-page h1s.

title.purpose: Serif h3s in rows, timeline steps and cards (28-36px; service index rows to 48px).

body.purpose: Lead paragraphs and section intros, about 36rem measure.

body-sm.purpose: Card text, FAQ answers, timeline copy.

label.purpose: Nav, metadata, chips, fact terms (13-15px), sentence case, no tracking.

button.purpose: Serif pill labels; 15px in compact pills.

data.purpose: Real machine output only: logs, timers, code.

shadows.name: hairline-ring
shadows.purpose: White cards on the ground: testimonial, image frames, rating chip.

shadows.name: lifted-panel
shadows.purpose: Cards resting on stone, e.g. the CTA chat card.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: Floating service preview; project images on hover (-40px spread, 0.45).

shadows.name: button-dark
shadows.purpose: Dark pill at rest; hover lengthens to 0 10px 24px -10px at .55.

shadows.name: button-light
shadows.purpose: Light pill ring at rest; hover firms to .3 with 0 10px 24px -14px at .35.

motion.name: ease-settle
motion.purpose: Reveals, headline lines, FAQ open, stage swaps, hover translations.

motion.name: ease-rise
motion.purpose: Hero copy and buttons rising in, 900ms.

motion.name: reveal
motion.value: opacity 0, translateY(28px), blur(8px) to rest over 1s
motion.purpose: Section content settling on scroll; siblings staggered 50-120ms; 2.5s safety reveal.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: all reveals, line-ins, stage swaps, marquee and wordmark pan disabled

conventions.data-ui: Interface fragments (laptop stage, principle scenes) carry the data-ui attribute; the depicted app's own styling governs inside them.

components.name: Dark Button
components.description: Primary pill: dark gradient with a cursor-following soft light. First of a dark/light pair.
components.css: .ds-btn { position: relative; isolation: isolate; overflow: hidden; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem; white-space: nowrap; border: 0; cursor: pointer; border-radius: 9999px; padding: 0.9rem 1.5rem; font-family: 'Source Serif 4 Variable', Georgia, serif; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: -0.005em; text-decoration: none; transition: box-shadow .35s cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1), transform .35s cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1); } .ds-btn::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 0; z-index: -1; opacity: 0; transition: opacity .35s cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1); background: radial-gradient(140px circle at 50% 50%, var(--ds-light), transparent 70%); } .ds-btn:hover::after { opacity: 1; } .ds-btn:active { transform: scale(.97); } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-btn-dark { --ds-light: oklch(1 0 0 / .22); color: var(--ink-foreground); background-image: linear-gradient(180deg, oklch(0.36 0.012 60) 0%, oklch(0.17 0.008 60) 100%); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 oklch(1 0 0 / .14), 0 1px 2px oklch(0.2 0.02 60 / .25); } .ds-btn-dark:hover { box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 oklch(1 0 0 / .18), 0 10px 24px -10px oklch(0.2 0.02 60 / .55); }

narrative.overview:
Kriyvo is presented with the calm polish of an AI product company. The page itself stays quiet: a near-white neutral ground, warm stone panels, near-black ink panels, a light serif display and a plain grotesk body. The noise is reserved for proof. Every service is drawn on the real screen it lives on (a laptop running the client's site, a chat widget, WhatsApp Web, an n8n canvas, a call console, a log stream) and those screens move, type and fill in as the visitor watches.

Density is generous. Sections sit 128–176px apart inside a 1240px container, headings are short and set in a regular-weight serif, and most surfaces are soft rounded panels separated by tone rather than lines or shadows. Orange is the brand, but it appears as signal, never as paint: a progress line, a filled timeline step, a rating star, a link, a check mark, the focus ring.

Motion is the second voice. Headline lines rise out of a blur one after another, sections settle from blur as they enter, the process timeline fills on scroll, project images tilt toward the cursor, and both button styles carry a soft light that follows the pointer. Everything respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral near-white ground with stone and ink panels; tone carries the hierarchy.
Source Serif 4 at about 360 for display, Host Grotesk for everything read, Geist Mono only for real data.
Orange held to signal; saffron for small highlights, mostly on ink.
Pill buttons in two finishes (dark gradient, light ringed) with a cursor-following light.
Product proof drawn as real interface fragments, marked with `data-ui`.
Heroes are type, two buttons and a quiet proof line: no glow blobs, no eyebrow pills.

rules.name: The Signal Orange Rule
rules.body: Flame and accent mark state, progress and links only. They never fill a panel, a section band or a headline, and never colour a primary button.

rules.name: The Saffron on Ink Rule
rules.body: Saffron is a highlight for small things (a tag, a chip, a numeral, an icon) and lives mostly on ink, where it reads warm without competing with flame.

rules.name: The Tone Not Grey Rule
rules.body: Secondary text is the body colour at reduced opacity (70%, 75%, 80%); on ink it is paper at 55–65%. Do not introduce new greys.

rules.name: The Quiet Serif Rule
rules.body: h1 and h2 are Source Serif 4 at 360 with tight tracking and balanced wrapping. Never set display type bold, uppercase or tracked out.

rules.name: The Real Data Mono Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono appears only where the content is actual machine output: logs, timers, code. It is never a decorative label face.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Prices, counts, step numbers and pagers use tabular figures so they do not jitter as they change.

rules.name: The One Dark Band Rule
rules.body: A page carries at most one full-bleed ink band (the about page's principles, a case study's results). Ink otherwise appears as contained panels.

rules.name: The Settle Rule
rules.body: Content enters by settling: 28px rise, 8px blur to sharp, opacity 0 to 1 over one second on an expo-out curve, staggered 50–120ms between siblings. Anything not revealed within 2.5s is shown regardless.

rules.name: The Tonal First Rule
rules.body: Reach for a tone step (ground, stone, card, ink) before a shadow. A shadow means "raised or active", never "this is a box".

rules.name: The Pill and Panel Rule
rules.body: Interactive controls are pills; containers are 22–28px panels. Do not mix in square-cornered boxes or small 4–8px card radii outside thumbnails and interface fragments.

rules.name: The Real Screen Rule
rules.body: Inside a `data-ui` fragment the depicted app's own styling governs: WhatsApp greens and bubble shadows, macOS window dots, a client site's tracked caps, 11–12px UI labels, mono log rows. Site-level rules about tracking, hex colours and the type scale apply outside fragments, not inside them.

dos: **Do** separate surfaces by tone (ground, stone, white, ink) before reaching for a border or shadow.
**Do** keep orange to signal: progress, live states, stars, links, check marks, focus.
**Do** open heroes with a serif headline of one or two lines, one sentence with real prices, a dark and a light pill, and a quiet proof line.
**Do** show a service on its real screen as a `data-ui` fragment rather than with an icon or an adjective.
**Do** use pills for every control and 22–28px radii for every panel.
**Do** let content settle from blur, stagger siblings by 50–120ms, and honour reduced motion.
donts: **Don't** place glow blobs, gradient orbs or blurred colour fields behind a hero.
**Don't** put eyebrow pills, kickers or tracked uppercase labels above headings.
**Don't** build grids of cards headed by icon tiles; show the work instead.
**Don't** fill panels, bands or primary buttons with flame or accent.
**Don't** set the display serif bold, uppercase or letter-spaced.
**Don't** use Geist Mono for labels, tags or decoration.
**Don't** use more than one full-bleed ink band on a page.
